newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso rises as dollar outflow fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso rises as dollar outflow fears ease.

text.p: The Philippine peso opened slightly up in range-bound trade on Wednesday as fears eased that there would be an outflow of dollars afterthe sharp drop in local share prices earlier this week, dealers said.
The peso was trading at 26.366/26.364 to the dollar from Tuesday's close of 26.368.
"I expect a firmer peso. There's still a lot of dollars in the market," said one dealer
The outflows may in fact have been no more than switching of funds from the stock market to fixed income secutiries,one dealer said.
Dealers said enthusiasm generated by the Philippine maiden 20-year treasury bond auction on Tuesday indicated confidence of investors in the economy.
The Central Bank pegged its bid/offer rates at 26.27/26.37.
Total volume reached $35.5 million after one hour of trade.
